figures.caption: Figure 6: Memory vs. Runtime Trade-off of TFLA Forward-Backward Pass. We show the mLSTMsig for embedding dimension 4096 (8 heads with dim 512), sequence length 8192 and batch size 8. By varying the chunk size parameter, TFLA kernels can effectively balance memory vs. runtime.
figures.label: Figure 6
figures.title: Memory vs. Runtime Trade-off of TFLA Forward-Backward Pass

numbered_list: (1) The chunk size L mediates a trade-off between runtime and GPU memory usage [Figure 6].
(2) L determines the total compute in FLOPs: L = 1 matches the recurrent formulation, while L = T matches the parallel one [Figure 19].
(3) There exists an optimal chunk size L ∈ [1, T] that minimized the total FLOP count [Equation (103), Figure 19, Figure 20].
(4) Increasing L raises the arithmetic intensity of TFLA kernels [Equation (109), Figure 22].
(5) The chunk size determines whether the kernel is memory-bound or compute-bound on a given hardware [Figure 23, Figure 22].
(6) FLOPs/s alone can be misleading; the optimal chunk size should be chosen based on total runtime [Figure 24, Figure 21].
(7) The runtime-optimal chunk size scales proportionally with the square root of the head dimension and the accelerator's computational intensity [Figure 25, Figure 26].
(8) Newer hardware generations require larger chunk sizes to approach peak performance. [Figure 26, Figure 21].

sections.content_summary: Discusses chunk size parameter L balancing computation between two levels of sequence parallelism; smaller chunks increase memory consumption but reduce quadratic compute FLOPs; larger chunks have opposite effect.
